- When sentiment is positive (≥0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward by 2–5% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) for 3+ consecutive days, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to counteract mean reversion bias.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply +1–2% bias to first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from positive to negative), model often lags; adjust forecast 1–3 days ahead to reflect sentiment shift.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term volatility; smooth out 3–5 day moving average of forecast to reduce noise.
